INK & BRASS

Editorial minimalism carrying the chowk metaphor — the square where a town's roads meet.

No glow, no glassmorphism, no gradient text. Hairline rules and air do the separating. Brass is the only accent on a page; indigo and terracotta appear once per viewport at most.

Type: Instrument Serif (display) + Instrument Sans (body) + JetBrains Mono (labels) + Tiro Devanagari Hindi (चौक).

Note: this swaps the Fraunces/Inter pairing from the plan — both are on the overused list and were pulling it back toward generic.

[BRACKETED TEXT] = a real fact I don't have yet.

Nothing on these boards is invented: no client names, no metrics, no testimonials, no star ratings, no 'trusted by 100+'. Every number that used to be on the site is gone rather than replaced with a smaller lie.

You fill in: city, month/year availability, author names and roles, reading times, cover images.

The blog post titles are drafted as examples of the voice — swap them for what you'd actually write.

LIGHT BRASS WAS DARKENED

The first pass used #9c6f2a, which lands at 4.16:1 on paper — under WCAG AA for normal text, and it was carrying small mono labels and every link.

Now #8f6425, at 4.89:1. Dark-mode brass (#d9a441 on ink, 8.4:1) was already fine and is unchanged.

Worth catching here: this token propagates into the whole build.

The game is a second door, never the only one. Every stall is also a normal crawlable route, and the first focusable element on the page is the escape hatch out of it (shown focused here). Reduced-motion visitors get the list and a 'start anyway' button rather than an auto-starting canvas.
